RUSS 121.description: Grammar and practical vocabulary necessary for fundamental communication skills. Assumes no prior experience in the language.
RUSS 121.subject: RUSS
RUSS 121.title: Elementary Russian

RUSS 122.description: Practice and further development of essential listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills.
RUSS 122.subject: RUSS
RUSS 122.title: Basic Proficiency in Russian

RUSS 201.description: Continued exposure to the fundamentals of Russian grammar, along with increased focus on reading and speaking skills.
RUSS 201.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 122 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 201.subject: RUSS
RUSS 201.title: Intermediate Russian I

RUSS 202.description: Completion of exposure to the fundamentals of Russian grammar, with emphasis on writing, reading, and conversation.
RUSS 202.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 201 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 202.subject: RUSS
RUSS 202.title: Intermediate Russian II

RUSS 280.description: A multimedia introduction to Russian culture from its beginnings to the present. No knowledge of Russian required.
RUSS 280.subject: RUSS
RUSS 280.title: Introduction to Russian Civilization

RUSS 298.description: Introductory-level study of selected topics in Russian culture. Does not apply toward the Russian major. May be repeated for credit under a different title.
RUSS 298.subject: RUSS
RUSS 298.title: Selected Topics

RUSS 301.description: Conversation, reading, composition, comprehensive review of grammar.
RUSS 301.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 202 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 301.subject: RUSS
RUSS 301.title: Russian Conversation and Composition I

RUSS 302.description: Emphasis on oral proficiency, using contemporary authentic materials from Russian newspapers, textbooks, and television newscasts.
RUSS 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 301 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 302.subject: RUSS
RUSS 302.title: Russian Conversation and Composition II

RUSS 319.description: Masterworks of Russian literature by Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Turgenev, Pushkin, Chekov, and others.
RUSS 319.subject: RUSS
RUSS 319.title: Nineteenth-Century Russian Literature in Translation

RUSS 319L.description: A Russian-language course designed to supplement 319. Reading and discussion in Russian of 19th-century poetry and prose.
RUSS 319L.subject: RUSS
RUSS 319L.title: Nineteenth-Century Russian Literature in Russian

RUSS 320.description: Masterworks of Russian literature by Bely, Pasternak, Bulgakov, Nabokov, Solzhenitsyn, and others.
RUSS 320.subject: RUSS
RUSS 320.title: Twentieth-Century Russian Literature in Translation

RUSS 320L.description: A Russian-language course designed to supplement RUSS 320 .
RUSS 320L.subject: RUSS
RUSS 320L.title: Twentieth-Century Russian Literature in Russian

RUSS 330.description: An introduction to the linguistic structure of Russian, with particular attention to phonology and morphology.
RUSS 330.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in RUSS 202 or by placement.
RUSS 330.subject: RUSS
RUSS 330.title: Structure of Russian

RUSS 340.description: An examination of Russian short stories and essays by Russian writers from the nineteenth century to the twenty-first century.
RUSS 340.subject: RUSS
RUSS 340.title: Russian Shorts: Stories and Essays

RUSS 350.description: An introduction to Russian fairy tales and other genres of folklore, both in their original form within an oral tradition and as reworked in Russian art and literature.
RUSS 350.subject: RUSS
RUSS 350.title: Russian Folklore and Fairy Tales

RUSS 398.description: Intensive study of selected topics in Russian cultural and/or literary movements. Taught in English. May be repeated for credit under a different title.
RUSS 398.subject: RUSS
RUSS 398.title: Selected Topics

RUSS 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
RUSS 399.subject: RUSS
RUSS 399.title: Independent Study

RUSS 401.description: Acquisition of subtleties of Russian grammar. Increased focus on reading, writing, and discussion.
RUSS 401.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 302 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 401.subject: RUSS
RUSS 401.title: Advanced Russian I

RUSS 402.description: Exposure to prose and poetry from a wide variety of sources and periods. Focus on oral proficiency, reading, comprehension, and writing.
RUSS 402.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: RUSS 401 or satisfactory score on language placement test.
RUSS 402.subject: RUSS
RUSS 402.title: Advanced Russian II

RUSS 498.description: Topics in Russian language and culture. Course conducted in Russian.
RUSS 498.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in RUSS 202.
RUSS 498.subject: RUSS
RUSS 498.title: Topics in Russian Language and Culture

RUSS 518.description: An introduction to the culture of medieval Russia through its written records, folklore, icons, and ancient religious chant.
RUSS 518.subject: RUSS
RUSS 518.title: Medieval Russian Culture

RUSS 520.description: An exploration of Russian modernist culture, with particular attention to the themes of social and political change. Authors under discussion include Kuzmin, Bely, and Zamyatin.
RUSS 520.subject: RUSS
RUSS 520.title: Russian Modernism: Love, Sex and Politics in Revolutionary Russia

RUSS 530.description: An examination of the influence of Homer’s epic poems The Iliad and The Odyssey on Russian culture, as seen in works by Russian writers including Tolstoy, Pasternak, and Brodsky.
RUSS 530.subject: RUSS
RUSS 530.title: Homer in Russia

RUSS 540.description: An examination of Russian writers reflecting on Russian national identity, including Solzhenitsyn, Dostoevsky, and Grossman.
RUSS 540.subject: RUSS
RUSS 540.title: Writing Russian National Identity

RUSS 598.description: Reading and research on selected topics in Russian. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title.
RUSS 598.subject: RUSS
RUSS 598.title: Selected Topics in Russian

RUSS 615.description: Intensive reading course for non-majors. Primarily for graduate students to fulfill the foreign- language reading requirement. It will not be applied toward the degree language requirements nor will it be accepted as a substitute in the course sequence leading to the various degree requirements.
RUSS 615.subject: RUSS
RUSS 615.title: Intensive Readings in Russian

RUSS 616.description: Intensive reading course for non-majors. Primarily for graduate students to fulfill the foreign-language reading requirement. It will not be applied toward the degree language requirements nor will it be accepted as a substitute in the course sequence leading to the various degree requirements.
RUSS 616.subject: RUSS
RUSS 616.title: Intensive Readings in Russian

RUSS 777.description: Supervised direction of foreign language teaching in college. Required of all graduate assistants who are teaching. This course will not count toward the MA or PhD degree.
RUSS 777.subject: RUSS
RUSS 777.title: Supervised Instruction in Teaching Foreign Languages in College
